items.stem: In the study of branches of geography and approaches to its study, the term 'biogeography' refers to:
items.answer: The branch of geography that studies the interface between the physical environment and human beings, including plant and animal geography and ecology
items.markingKey: (c) 'biogeography' means the branch of geography that studies the interface between the physical environment and human beings, including plant and animal geography and ecology.
options: The study of the earth as the home of human beings, concerned with the description and explanation of the areal differentiation of the earth's surface
A natural feature of the earth's surface, such as a mountain, plateau, plain or valley
The branch of geography that studies the interface between the physical environment and human beings, including plant and animal geography and ecology
The study of phenomena as they change over time, which is the central concern of history

items.stem:
Read the following statements about interpretation of satellite imageries:
I. Shadows help in identifying the height and shape of tall objects.
II. Pattern refers to the spatial arrangement of objects, such as orchards in rows.
III. Tone refers to the outline of an object.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and II only
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct. III is incorrect: Tone is relative brightness or colour; shape is the outline.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the formation of planets and the moon is correct?
items.answer: The planets were formed in three stages: stars formed in a nebula, planetesimals condensed, and planetesimals collided and accreted into planets.
items.markingKey: (c) The others are wrong: It is believed to have formed after a giant impact of a Mars-sized body with the earth. Jupiter is a Jovian planet. The terrestrial planets are rocky; Jovian planets are gas giants.
options: The moon was formed from a piece of the sun.
The Jovian planets are made mainly of rock and metal.
The planets were formed in three stages: stars formed in a nebula, planetesimals condensed, and planetesimals collided and accreted into planets.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the Peninsular drainage and its evolution:
I. Short west-flowing rivers of the west coast include the Sharavati and the Periyar.
II. The Kaveri rises on the Amarkantak plateau.
III. The Sabarmati and the Mahi drain into the Gulf of Khambhat.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and III only
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is incorrect: The Kaveri rises in the Brahmagiri hills; the Narmada rises at Amarkantak. III is correct.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the structure of the earth is NOT correct?
items.answer: The lithosphere includes the entire mantle.
items.markingKey: (d) It is incorrect. It includes the crust and only the uppermost solid part of the mantle.
options: The crust under the major mountain systems, such as the Himalayas, is about 70 km thick.
The crust is thicker under the continents than under the oceans.
The mantle extends from the Moho discontinuity to a depth of 2,900 km.
The lithosphere includes the entire mantle.

items.stem: Most waves in the ocean are caused by:
items.answer: wind
items.markingKey: (c) wind.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the essentials of maps and the difference between maps and sketches is NOT correct?
items.answer: Map projection is the ratio between map and ground distance.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. That is the scale; projection transforms the globe onto a plane.
options: Map projection is the ratio between map and ground distance.
The process of map making includes generalisation, map design, construction and production.
A map must have a title, a scale, a north direction and a legend of symbols.
Every map is a reduced representation of the earth's surface.

items.stem: Identify the place from the clue: The forest in Gujarat that is the home of the Asiatic lion.
items.answer: Gir
items.markingKey: (c) Gir: the forest in Gujarat that is the home of the Asiatic lion.

items.stem: To convert a statement of scale into a representative fraction, the ground distance must be:
items.answer: converted into the same unit as the map distance
items.markingKey: (b) converted into the same unit as the map distance.
options: converted into the same unit as the map distance

items.stem: In the study of plate tectonics and the movement of the Indian plate, the term 'convergent boundary' refers to:
items.answer: A boundary where one plate sinks under another and crust is destroyed, also called a subduction zone
items.markingKey: (b) 'convergent boundary' means a boundary where one plate sinks under another and crust is destroyed, also called a subduction zone.
options: Sedimentary rock formed out of deposits of glaciers, whose counterparts are found in India and other southern continents
A boundary where one plate sinks under another and crust is destroyed, also called a subduction zone
A boundary where plates slide past each other and crust is neither produced nor destroyed
The theory of Arthur Holmes that heat differences in the mantle create convection currents that move the crust

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the forces affecting the velocity and direction of wind:
I. Friction is greatest at the earth's surface and is least over the sea surface.
II. The Coriolis force is absent at the equator.
III. The Coriolis force is directly proportional to the angle of latitude.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: All of them
items.markingKey: (a) I is correct. II is correct. III is correct.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? Forces that originate within the earth and build up parts of the earth's surface.
items.answer: endogenic forces
items.markingKey: (c) endogenic forces: forces that originate within the earth and build up parts of the earth's surface.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about unity and diversity in the monsoon climate of India is NOT correct?
items.answer: Temperature conditions are uniform all over India.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. Temperatures range from about 55°C in western Rajasthan in summer to minus 45°C around Leh in winter.
options: Most parts of India get rain between June and September.
Temperature conditions are uniform all over India.
The climate of India shows regional diversity in temperature, winds and rainfall.
Mawsynram and Cherrapunji in the Khasi hills receive more than 1,000 cm of rainfall a year, while Jaisalmer rarely gets more than 9 cm.

items.stem: In which year did the following take place: Mercator's projection devised by Gerardus Mercator?
items.markingKey: (c) Mercator's projection devised by Gerardus Mercator took place in 1569.

items.stem: Settlements found along a road or river in a line show a:
items.answer: linear pattern
items.markingKey: (a) linear pattern.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The Himalayas are prone to earthquakes.
Reason (R): They are young fold mountains that are still rising due to the movement of the Indian plate.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: they are young fold mountains that are still rising due to the movement of the Indian plate.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Barchans have their wings pointing towards the wind.
Reason (R): There is little vegetation and loose dry material can be easily moved.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Their wings point away from the wind direction, downwind. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Weather changes quickly, even within a day or week. Climate changes very slowly and may remain unchanged for 50 years or more. The main elements of weather and climate are temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, clouds and precipitation. The elements of weather and climate are interrelated."
(i) Explain the term 'elements of weather', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The climate of a place changes very slowly. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Latitude is an element of weather." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) Temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, clouds and precipitation, which together describe weather and climate. (ii) It is the average of weather conditions over a long period of time. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Latitude is a factor controlling climate, not an element of weather.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) Temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, clouds and precipitation, which together describe weather and climate. (ii) It is the average of weather conditions over a long period of time. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Latitude is a factor controlling climate, not an element of weather.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"Out of 100 units of insolation, 27 units are reflected from the top of the clouds and 2 units from snow and ice-covered areas. The earth's surface absorbs 51 units of insolation and radiates the same amount back as terrestrial radiation. The earth as a whole does not accumulate or lose heat; it maintains its temperature. There is a surplus of net radiation in the tropics and a deficit near the poles."
(i) Explain the term 'heat surplus', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Out of 100 units, only 65 units actually heat the earth system. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The earth keeps getting warmer because it absorbs more heat than it loses." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) The excess of incoming over outgoing radiation, found between about 40° north and 40° south. (ii) 35 units are reflected back to space before reaching the surface or from snow and clouds. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Over a long period, incoming and outgoing radiation balance and the earth's temperature remains constant.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The excess of incoming over outgoing radiation, found between about 40° north and 40° south. (ii) 35 units are reflected back to space before reaching the surface or from snow and clouds. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Over a long period, incoming and outgoing radiation balance and the earth's temperature remains constant.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to standard time, time zones and the International Date Line.
(a) Give a reason for the following: The International Date Line is not a straight line. (1)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "Crossing the Date Line from east to west, a traveller repeats a day." (2)
items.answer: (a) It bends to avoid dividing countries and island groups into two dates. (b) He gains a day (the date advances); crossing west to east, he repeats a day.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (a) 1 for the reason – it bends to avoid dividing countries and island groups into two dates. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – He gains a day (the date advances); crossing west to east, he repeats a day. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: In the afternoon, air can hold 20 g/m³ of water vapour and contains 8 g/m³. At night it cools and its capacity falls to 16 g/m³ with no change in moisture. Calculate the relative humidity in the afternoon and at night, and explain the change.
items.answer: Afternoon RH = 8 ÷ 20 × 100 = 40%. Night RH = 8 ÷ 16 × 100 = 50%. Relative humidity rises at night because cooler air can hold less moisture, though absolute humidity is unchanged.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for each relative humidity value, 1 for explaining that capacity falls with temperature.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to the size of India and its neighbours.
(a) Give a reason for the following: The Himalayas form a natural frontier in the north. (1)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "India is the second largest country of the world by area." (2)
items.answer: (a) These young fold mountains are high and difficult to cross. (b) India is the seventh largest country by area.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: (a) 1 for the reason – these young fold mountains are high and difficult to cross. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – India is the seventh largest country by area. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Explain three factors that affect the salinity of ocean water.
items.answer: Evaporation and precipitation; fresh water inflow from rivers; freezing and thawing of ice; winds and ocean currents.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Evaporation and precipitation; fresh water inflow from rivers; freezing and thawing of ice; winds and ocean currents.

items.stem: Explain the branches of geography based on the systematic and regional approaches.
items.answer: Systematic – physical (geomorphology, climatology, hydrology, soil), human (social/cultural, population and settlement, economic, historical, political), biogeography (plant, zoo, ecology, environmental); regional – regional studies, planning, development, analysis; Humboldt and Ritter.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Systematic – physical (geomorphology, climatology, hydrology, soil), human (social/cultural, population and settlement, economic, historical, political), biogeography (plant, zoo, ecology, environmental); regional – regional studies, planning, development, analysis; Humboldt and Ritter.

items.stem: Explain the stages of remote sensing and the role of the electromagnetic spectrum.
items.answer: Stages – source, propagation, interaction, return propagation, detection, data products, information extraction, maps; spectrum – gamma to radio, visible 0.4–0.7 µm, infrared, microwave; spectral signatures – vegetation bright in near-infrared, water dark; applications.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Stages – source, propagation, interaction, return propagation, detection, data products, information extraction, maps; spectrum – gamma to radio, visible 0.4–0.7 µm, infrared, microwave; spectral signatures – vegetation bright in near-infrared, water dark; applications.

items.stem: Describe the early and modern theories of the origin of the earth and the universe.
items.answer: Nebular hypothesis (Kant, Laplace 1796); planetesimal (Chamberlain and Moulton 1900); revised nebular (Otto Schmidt, Weizascar 1950); Big Bang – tiny ball, explosion, expansion, 13.7 billion years; Hubble 1920; formation of galaxies and stars.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Nebular hypothesis (Kant, Laplace 1796); planetesimal (Chamberlain and Moulton 1900); revised nebular (Otto Schmidt, Weizascar 1950); Big Bang – tiny ball, explosion, expansion, 13.7 billion years; Hubble 1920; formation of galaxies and stars.

items.stem: Describe the Peninsular drainage system.
items.answer: Western Ghats as divide; east-flowing – Mahanadi (Sihawa), Godavari (Nasik, largest, Dakshin Ganga), Krishna (Mahabaleshwar), Kaveri (Brahmagiri, more even flow), deltas; west-flowing – Narmada (Amarkantak, rift valley, Dhuandhar), Tapi (Multai), Sabarmati, Mahi, Sharavati (Jog Falls), Periyar, estuaries; evolution.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Western Ghats as divide; east-flowing – Mahanadi (Sihawa), Godavari (Nasik, largest, Dakshin Ganga), Krishna (Mahabaleshwar), Kaveri (Brahmagiri, more even flow), deltas; west-flowing – Narmada (Amarkantak, rift valley, Dhuandhar), Tapi (Multai), Sabarmati, Mahi, Sharavati (Jog Falls), Periyar, estuaries; evolution.

items.stem: Describe the direct and indirect sources of information about the interior of the earth.
items.answer: Direct – mines, deep drilling projects, volcanic magma; indirect – temperature, pressure and density with depth; meteors; gravity and gravity anomalies; magnetic surveys; seismic activity as most important source.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Direct – mines, deep drilling projects, volcanic magma; indirect – temperature, pressure and density with depth; meteors; gravity and gravity anomalies; magnetic surveys; seismic activity as most important source.

items.stem:
On an outline map of the world, locate and label the following places (described below) related to movements of ocean water:
A. A bay in Canada that has the highest tides in the world
B. A cold current along the south-west coast of Africa
C. A cold current flowing south along the north-west coast of Africa
D. A cold current flowing north along the west coast of South America, also called the Humboldt Current
E. Rich fishing grounds off Newfoundland where the Gulf Stream and the Labrador Current meet
items.answer: A – Bay of Fundy; B – Benguela Current; C – Canaries Current; D – Peru Current; E – Grand Banks
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for correctly identifying and labelling: A – Bay of Fundy; B – Benguela Current; C – Canaries Current; D – Peru Current; E – Grand Banks.

items.stem:
On an outline political map of India, locate and label the following places (described below) related to the natural vegetation of India:
A. A national park in Assam known for the one-horned rhinoceros
B. A marine biosphere reserve between India and Sri Lanka
C. A high-altitude biosphere reserve in Uttarakhand
D. The forest in Gujarat that is the home of the Asiatic lion
E. The mangrove forests of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, home of the Royal Bengal tiger
items.answer: A – Kaziranga; B – Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve; C – Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve; D – Gir; E – Sundarbans
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for correctly identifying and labelling: A – Kaziranga; B – Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve; C – Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve; D – Gir; E – Sundarbans.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? The outer planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, which are gas giants.
items.answer: Jovian planets
items.markingKey: (c) Jovian planets: the outer planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, which are gas giants.

items.stem: The Peninsular river that has comparatively less seasonal fluctuation in flow because it gets both south-west and north-east monsoon rain is the:
items.answer: Kaveri
items.markingKey: (b) Kaveri.

items.stem:

I. In a convex slope, contours are widely spaced at the top and closely spaced at the bottom.
II. Contours often cross each other.
III. Closely spaced contours indicate a gentle slope.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I only
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is incorrect: They do not cross except at an overhanging cliff. III is incorrect: Closely spaced contours indicate a steep slope.

items.stem: A projection in which areas are correctly represented is called:

items.answer: geostrophic winds

items.stem: In the English system, 1 mile equals:
items.answer: 63,360 inches

items.answer: October heat

items.answer: near the mid-oceanic ridges

items.answer: Indira Point

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"A combination of basic cloud types gives forms such as cumulonimbus and stratocumulus. Mist contains more moisture than fog. Fogs are mini clouds in which condensation takes place around nuclei provided by dust, smoke and salt particles. Clouds are masses of minute water droplets or tiny ice crystals formed by condensation of water vapour in free air at considerable height."
(i) Explain the term 'cirrus', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Dew forms on calm, clear nights. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Fog contains more moisture than mist." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) High clouds formed at 8,000–12,000 m that are thin, detached and feathery. (ii) The ground loses heat quickly and cools the air in contact to its dew point. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Mist contains more moisture than fog.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) High clouds formed at 8,000–12,000 m that are thin, detached and feathery. (ii) The ground loses heat quickly and cools the air in contact to its dew point. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Mist contains more moisture than fog.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Luni is the main river of the Indian desert. The Indian desert has features such as shifting sand dunes, mushroom rocks and oases. The Western Ghats are higher and more continuous than the Eastern Ghats. The eastern coastal plain is broader than the western and has well-developed deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri."
(i) Explain the term 'Western Ghats', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The eastern coastal plain has large deltas. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Anaimudi is the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) The continuous range along the western edge of the Deccan plateau, also called the Sahyadri, higher than the Eastern Ghats. (ii) Big rivers such as the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri flow across it into the Bay of Bengal. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Anaimudi is the highest peak of Peninsular India; Mahendragiri is the highest of the Eastern Ghats.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The continuous range along the western edge of the Deccan plateau, also called the Sahyadri, higher than the Eastern Ghats. (ii) Big rivers such as the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri flow across it into the Bay of Bengal. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: Anaimudi is the highest peak of Peninsular India; Mahendragiri is the highest of the Eastern Ghats.

items.stem:

(a) Give a reason for the following: Plant life in valley bottoms may be damaged by frost on winter nights. (1)

items.answer: (a) Cold dense air drains down the slopes at night and collects in the valleys. (b) It occurs on long winter nights with clear skies and still air.

items.stem: What is karst topography? Name its erosional landforms.
items.answer: Landforms formed by groundwater on limestone or dolomite (Karst region, Balkans); erosional – sinkholes, swallow holes, dolines, uvalas, lapies, caves.

items.stem: Classify maps on the basis of function, with examples.
items.answer: Physical maps – relief, geological, climatic, soil, vegetation; cultural maps – political, population, economic, transportation.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Physical maps – relief, geological, climatic, soil, vegetation; cultural maps – political, population, economic, transportation.

items.stem: Compare the Himalayan and Peninsular rivers.
items.answer: Origin – Himalayas vs plateau; flow – perennial vs seasonal; valleys – gorges and V-shaped vs broad shallow; nature – youthful, antecedent vs mature, graded; courses – meanders, shifting vs fixed; basins – large vs small; deltas and estuaries.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Origin – Himalayas vs plateau; flow – perennial vs seasonal; valleys – gorges and V-shaped vs broad shallow; nature – youthful, antecedent vs mature, graded; courses – meanders, shifting vs fixed; basins – large vs small; deltas and estuaries.

items.stem: Compare the cylindrical equal area projection with Mercator's projection.
items.answer: Both cylindrical, parallels and meridians straight at right angles; equal area (Lambert) – correct area, parallels closer towards poles, pole a line equal to equator, shape distorted, tropical distributions; Mercator (1569) – orthomorphic, parallel spacing increases polewards, loxodromes straight, navigation, areas exaggerated, poles not shown.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Both cylindrical, parallels and meridians straight at right angles; equal area (Lambert) – correct area, parallels closer towards poles, pole a line equal to equator, shape distorted, tropical distributions; Mercator (1569) – orthomorphic, parallel spacing increases polewards, loxodromes straight, navigation, areas exaggerated, poles not shown.

items.stem: 'Geography is a discipline of synthesis.' Explain.
items.answer: Study of earth as home of humans; areal differentiation (Hartshorne); spatial synthesis vs temporal synthesis; links with natural and social sciences; physical–human interrelationships; 'what, where, why'.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Study of earth as home of humans; areal differentiation (Hartshorne); spatial synthesis vs temporal synthesis; links with natural and social sciences; physical–human interrelationships; 'what, where, why'.

items.stem: Explain the vertical and horizontal distribution of atmospheric pressure.
items.answer: Vertical – pressure decreases with height, about 1 mb per 10 m; sea-level average 1,013.2 mb; horizontal – isobars, pressure reduced to sea level; belts – equatorial low, subtropical highs (30°), sub-polar lows (60°), polar highs; seasonal shifting with the sun.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Vertical – pressure decreases with height, about 1 mb per 10 m; sea-level average 1,013.2 mb; horizontal – isobars, pressure reduced to sea level; belts – equatorial low, subtropical highs (30°), sub-polar lows (60°), polar highs; seasonal shifting with the sun.

items.stem: What are tides? Explain their causes, types and importance.
items.answer: Periodic rise and fall of sea level; gravitational pull of moon and sun, centrifugal force; tidal bulges; types by frequency – semi-diurnal, diurnal, mixed; by sun-moon-earth positions – spring and neap; perigee and perihelion; Bay of Fundy; importance – navigation, fishing, desilting, tidal energy.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Periodic rise and fall of sea level; gravitational pull of moon and sun, centrifugal force; tidal bulges; types by frequency – semi-diurnal, diurnal, mixed; by sun-moon-earth positions – spring and neap; perigee and perihelion; Bay of Fundy; importance – navigation, fishing, desilting, tidal energy.

items.stem:
On an outline political map of India, locate and label the following places (described below) related to the climate of India:
A. A west-coast city that gets heavy rain from the Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon
B. A place in western Rajasthan that rarely gets more than 9 cm of rain in a year
C. A city where violent summer thunderstorms called Kalbaisakhi occur
D. A place in the Khasi hills of Meghalaya that receives among the highest rainfall in the world
E. A place in the cold desert of Ladakh where winter temperatures drop very low
items.answer: A – Mumbai; B – Jaisalmer; C – Kolkata; D – Mawsynram; E – Leh
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for correctly identifying and labelling: A – Mumbai; B – Jaisalmer; C – Kolkata; D – Mawsynram; E – Leh.

items.stem:
On an outline political map of India, locate and label the following places (described below) related to the natural vegetation of India:
A. The forest in Gujarat that is the home of the Asiatic lion
B. A high-altitude biosphere reserve in Uttarakhand
C. A marine biosphere reserve between India and Sri Lanka
D. The first biosphere reserve of India, at the junction of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka
E. A biosphere reserve in Odisha
items.answer: A – Gir; B – Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve; C – Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve; D – Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve; E – Simlipal
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for correctly identifying and labelling: A – Gir; B – Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve; C – Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve; D – Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve; E – Simlipal.

items.stem: Which term describes the following? A relatively rapid and perceptible movement of debris down a slope.
items.answer: landslide
items.markingKey: (b) landslide: a relatively rapid and perceptible movement of debris down a slope.

items.stem: Which of the following seas has higher salinity than the open ocean?
items.answer: Mediterranean Sea
items.markingKey: (b) Mediterranean Sea.

items.stem:
Read the following statements about the composition of the atmosphere:
I. Water vapour absorbs part of the insolation and also preserves the earth's radiated heat.
II. Dust particles are most concentrated in the upper atmosphere.
III. Dust particles are generally concentrated in the lower layers of the atmosphere.
Which of these statements are correct?
items.answer: I and III only
items.markingKey: (d) I is correct. II is incorrect: They are concentrated in the lower layers of the atmosphere. III is correct.

items.stem: In the study of earthquakes and earthquake waves, the term 'Richter scale' refers to:
items.answer: The scale that measures the magnitude, or energy released, of an earthquake, from 0 to 10
items.markingKey: (d) 'Richter scale' means the scale that measures the magnitude, or energy released, of an earthquake, from 0 to 10.

items.stem: Identify the place from the clue: A peak in the Nilgiri hills.
items.answer: Doddabetta
items.markingKey: (a) Doddabetta: a peak in the Nilgiri hills.

items.stem: Which of the following is a cold current?
items.answer: Labrador Current
items.markingKey: (a) Labrador Current.

items.stem: In the study of the importance of physical geography, the term 'natural resources' refers to:
items.answer: Materials from the environment such as soil, water, forests and minerals that people use
items.markingKey: (a) 'natural resources' means materials from the environment such as soil, water, forests and minerals that people use.
options: Materials from the environment such as soil, water, forests and minerals that people use

items.stem: Fog mixed with smoke is called:
items.answer: smog
items.markingKey: (b) smog.

items.stem: In the study of drainage systems, drainage patterns and drainage basins, the term 'centripetal pattern' refers to:
items.answer: A drainage pattern in which rivers flow into a central depression or lake from all directions, as into the Loktak lake
items.markingKey: (c) 'centripetal pattern' means a drainage pattern in which rivers flow into a central depression or lake from all directions, as into the Loktak lake.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the factors determining India's climate is NOT correct?
items.answer: Western disturbances originate over the Bay of Bengal.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. They originate over the Mediterranean Sea.
options: Relief influences rainfall, as on the windward Western Ghats compared with the leeward Deccan.
The heating of the Tibetan plateau in summer influences the monsoon.
Western disturbances originate over the Bay of Bengal.
Western disturbances are brought into India by the westerly jet stream in winter.

items.stem:
Statement: Isotherms bend northwards over the North Atlantic in January.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: The warm North Atlantic Drift raises the temperature of the ocean and nearby coasts.
items.markingKey: (b) The warm North Atlantic Drift raises the temperature of the ocean and nearby coasts.
options: It is far from the moderating influence of the sea (continentality).
The warm North Atlantic Drift raises the temperature of the ocean and nearby coasts.
The southern hemisphere has a much larger proportion of oceans, which heat and cool uniformly.
The amount of heat received as insolation equals the amount lost by terrestrial radiation.

items.stem: Identifying a school by the presence of a playground nearby uses the element of:
items.answer: association
items.markingKey: (b) association.

items.stem: In the study of landforms made by running water, the term 'canyon' refers to:
items.answer: A valley with steep step-like side slopes, wider at the top than at the bottom
items.markingKey: (a) 'canyon' means a valley with steep step-like side slopes, wider at the top than at the bottom.
options: A valley with steep step-like side slopes, wider at the top than at the bottom
A steep rocky face along a high coast formed by wave erosion
A smooth, oval-shaped ridge of glacial till, with its blunt end facing the direction of ice movement
A long, narrow to wide trench formed when several sinkholes merge

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the classification of map projections is correct?
items.answer: Zenithal projections may be polar, equatorial or oblique depending on where the plane touches the globe.
items.markingKey: (d) The others are wrong: It preserves correct shape; homolographic preserves area. That is a zenithal projection; conical projections use a cone. It has the light at the centre of the globe; orthographic has it at infinity.

items.stem: The remains of Mesosaurus, a small reptile, are found in South Africa and:
items.answer: Brazil
items.markingKey: (c) Brazil.

items.stem:

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"A tornado over the sea is called a water spout. Thunderstorms are caused by intense convection on moist hot days. Extra-tropical cyclones cover a larger area than tropical cyclones. Tropical cyclones need a continuous supply of moisture and lose strength after landfall."
(i) Explain the term 'eye', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Fronts bring changes in weather. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Extra-tropical cyclones move from east to west." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) The calm central region of a mature tropical cyclone with subsiding air. (ii) Warm air is forced to rise over cold air along them, causing clouds and precipitation. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: They move from west to east with the westerlies.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The calm central region of a mature tropical cyclone with subsiding air. (ii) Warm air is forced to rise over cold air along them, causing clouds and precipitation. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: They move from west to east with the westerlies.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The southern part of India lies within the tropics and the northern part lies in the sub-tropical and warm temperate zone. There is a time lag of about two hours between Arunachal Pradesh in the east and Gujarat in the west. The east-west extent of India appears smaller than its north-south extent because the distance between meridians decreases towards the poles. The latitudinal and longitudinal extent of the mainland of India is about 30 degrees each."
(i) Explain the term 'Standard Meridian of India', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: India has a great diversity in climate. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "The Standard Meridian of India is 80°30' E." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (1)
items.answer: (i) The meridian of 82°30' E, passing through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh, on which Indian Standard Time is based. (ii) It extends over about 30 degrees of latitude, with the south in the tropics and the north in the sub-tropical zone. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It is 82°30' E, passing through Mirzapur.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) The meridian of 82°30' E, passing through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh, on which Indian Standard Time is based. (ii) It extends over about 30 degrees of latitude, with the south in the tropics and the north in the sub-tropical zone. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: It is 82°30' E, passing through Mirzapur.

items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for vertical interval, 1 for horizontal equivalent from the scale, 1 for the gradient.

items.stem: Name and explain any three essentials of a map.
items.answer: Scale – ratio of map to ground distance; projection – globe onto plane; generalisation – selection by purpose; symbolisation – conventional signs; orientation – north direction.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Scale – ratio of map to ground distance; projection – globe onto plane; generalisation – selection by purpose; symbolisation – conventional signs; orientation – north direction.

items.stem: Explain the three methods of expressing scale.
items.answer: Statement – in words (1 cm represents 10 km); representative fraction – ratio without units (1:100,000); graphical – divided line, valid on enlargement and reduction.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Statement – in words (1 cm represents 10 km); representative fraction – ratio without units (1:100,000); graphical – divided line, valid on enlargement and reduction.

items.stem: Describe the stages in the formation of planets.
items.answer: Stars as lumps of gas within the nebula; gravitational force forms a core and gas disc; condensation into small rounded planetesimals; collisions and accretion form a few large planets.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: Stars as lumps of gas within the nebula; gravitational force forms a core and gas disc; condensation into small rounded planetesimals; collisions and accretion form a few large planets.

items.stem: Explain the endogenic processes that shape the earth's surface.
items.answer: Endogenic vs exogenic forces; source of energy; diastrophism – orogeny, epeirogeny, earthquakes, plate tectonics; volcanism; effects on relief.
items.markingKey: 5 marks: credit each relevant point explained with NCERT evidence – Endogenic vs exogenic forces; source of energy; diastrophism – orogeny, epeirogeny, earthquakes, plate tectonics; volcanism; effects on relief.

items.stem: Describe the major relief features of the ocean floor.
items.answer: Continental shelf – shallow, average 80 km wide, absent off Chile, Siberian shelf largest; continental slope – steep; deep sea plain – flattest, 3,000–6,000 m; oceanic deeps – trenches, most in Pacific, Mariana; minor features – ridges, seamounts, guyots, canyons, atolls.

items.stem: Describe the composition of the atmosphere.
items.answer: Gases – nitrogen about 78%, oxygen about 21%, argon, carbon dioxide (greenhouse gas, rising due to fossil fuels), ozone (10–50 km, absorbs UV); water vapour – up to 4% in warm wet tropics, less in cold dry areas, decreases with height, absorbs and preserves heat; dust particles – lower layers, more in subtropical and temperate areas, hygroscopic nuclei.

items.stem: Describe earthquake waves and the effects of earthquakes.
items.answer: Focus and epicentre; body waves – P (fastest, all media) and S (solids only); surface waves (most destructive); shadow zones; types of earthquakes; Richter and Mercalli scales; effects – shaking, landslides, liquefaction, fires, tsunamis.

items.stem: Describe the regional divisions of the Himalayas and the main features of the northern plain.
items.answer: Kashmir Himalayas – Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar, Pir Panjal, karewas, passes; Himachal–Uttarakhand – duns; Darjiling–Sikkim – duars, tea; Arunachal – Namcha Barwa; eastern hills – Patkai, Naga, Manipur, Mizo hills, Loktak; northern plain – bhabar, terai, bhangar, khadar, alluvial fertility.
